The real demonstrative resumes that immediately stated self-commender within the single subject/predicate construction; no independent Greek relative or second person is invented.
Actual heauton is the printed third-person accusative-masculine-singular reflexive, rendered himself as the commending object.

Actual synistanōn is present active nominative-singular commending participle, expanded is-commending without a written finite being verb. It is distinct from the later real finite commending predicate.
Actual estin is the separately written present active third-person-singular being predicate and owns the second English is, not the participle auxiliary.
Actual dokimos is nominative-masculine-singular approved/tested adjective, not a source approving participle.
Actual hon is accusative-masculine-singular relative of the Lord’s commending object, expanded he-whom with actual accusative retained.
Actual synistēsin is present active third-person-singular commending predicate, owning commends with its own source position distinct from the earlier participle.
